name: Sigbjørn Obstfelder
credit: Portrait of Sigbjørn Obstfelder (1900) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Sigbjørn Obstfelder (1866–1900) was a Norwegian poet and prose writer, born in Stavanger. He trained as an engineer, spent some years in the United States in the late 1880s, and then settled in Kristiania (Oslo) and Copenhagen, where he devoted himself to writing.

His only lifetime book of verse, Digte (1893), broke with rhymed and metrical convention in favour of short, free, strangely hesitant lines that express a sense of being a stranger on earth. He died of tuberculosis in Copenhagen in 1900, aged thirty-three, and is regarded as a forerunner of modernism in Scandinavian poetry.

poems.title: Jeg ser
poems.author: Sigbjørn Obstfelder
poems.text:
Jeg ser paa den hvide himmel,
jeg ser paa de graablaa skyer,
jeg ser paa den blodige sol.

Dette er altsaa verden.
Dette er altsaa klodernes hjem.

En regndraabe!

Jeg ser paa de høie huse,
jeg ser paa de tusende vinduer,
jeg ser paa det fjerne kirketaarn.

Dette er altsaa jorden.
Dette er altsaa menneskenes hjem.

De graablaa skyer samler sig. solen blev borte.

Jeg ser paa de velklædte herrer,
jeg ser paa de smilende damer,
jeg ser paa de ludende heste.

Hvor de graablaa skyer blir tunge.

Jeg ser, jeg ser....
Jeg er vist kommet paa en feil klode!
Her er saa underligt...

poems.title: Nocturne
poems.author: Sigbjørn Obstfelder
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Scandinavian Verse (1925)
poems.text:
Møllens vinger stanser sin susen,
Aaen speiler nattens øie,
Blomsternes læber ydmygt beder,
Træernes kroner hvisker, hvisker.

Presterne tænder de blege kjerter,
Nonnerne nynner de fromme bønner,
Børnene folder de spinkle hænder,
Svanerne skjuler sit neb under vingen.

Snart skal de sove, alle de trætte,
Hvile hodet mygt paa puden,
Glemme de graa, sorgmodige tanker,
Slumre, sove, drømme, sove.
